sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Rails migrations are how the schema evolves, and the interview questions go well beyond 'how do you add a column'. The most important production topic is zero-downtime migrations — the add/backfill/remove three-step for adding a NOT NULL column to a large table without locking it. This page covers the change method and when to use up/down instead, the reversible do block for non-reversible DDL, the schema.rb vs structure.sql choice (use structure.sql when you use DB-specific features like partial indexes, triggers, or custom types), adding indexes (including expression indexes and partial indexes), the strong_migrations gem for catching dangerous migrations in CI, and running migrations safely in a blue-green or rolling deployment.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: migration-patterns, zero-downtime, schema-and-structure-sql, indexes. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
